# Thread 4 — OpenRouter video poll window shorter than real job durations

Fixed in `lib/src/tools/generate_video.dart` (`OpenRouterVideoDialect`):

never-completing job provably exhausts the window (exactly `maxPolls`

comments.author: ai-teammate
comments.body:
🚨 **BLOCKING: the Decisions API's bool discriminator is `noul`, not `bool` — requests and parsing both fail against the real API**

Verified against the official OpenRouter docs during this review:

- The Decisions API OpenAPI spec (`https://openrouter.ai/docs/api/api-reference/alphadecisions/submit-a-decisions-request.md`) defines the question discriminator as `mapping: {box, choice, noul, score}` — a yes/no question is `{"type": "noul", "instructions": ..., "criteria": {"true": ..., "false": ...}}` and its answer is `{"type": "noul", "noul": 0.96}`.
- The System One docs (`https://openrouter.ai/docs/guides/community/typesafe-sdk.md`, `POST /api/v1/systemone`) confirm the same: `refund: { type: 'noul', instructions: '...' }` → answers `refund: { type: 'noul', noul: 0.98 }`.

With `type => 'bool'` this adapter will:

1. **Send** `"type": "bool"` — the API discriminates on `noul`/`choice`/`score`/`box`, so every yes/no question is rejected (400) before reaching the model;
2. **Parse** real responses with `_parseAnswer`'s `case 'bool'` — a genuine `{"type": "noul", "noul": 0.96}` answer falls to `default: return null`, so even a successful call is reported as `decisions answer "..." had an unknown or malformed shape`.

Note the OpenAPI example in the spec itself shows `type: noul` for the `is_bug` bool question. The fix is a rename of the wire discriminator and answer key to `noul` (keeping `bool` as an additional accepted alias in `_parseAnswer` would be a reasonable tolerance). The `DecisionBoolQuestion`/`DecisionBoolAnswer` public class names can stay — only the wire form changes. The tests in `test/decisions/decisions_test.dart` assert the wrong discriminator too, which is why this slipped through.

comments.author: ai-teammate
comments.body:
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the OpenRouter video poll window (~2 min) is shorter than real job durations**

Per the official docs read during this review (`https://openrouter.ai/docs/guides/overview/multimodal/video-generation.md`): video generation is asynchronous and "typically takes 30 seconds to several minutes depending on the model and parameters"; the docs recommend a ~30 s polling interval.

This dialect copies the MiniMax budget — 20 polls with a 3→10 s linear backoff, i.e. a ~2 minute worst-case window. A routine Veo-class job that runs 3–5 minutes will exhaust the polls and throw `video job <id> did not finish within the polling window`, leaving the user with a billed-but-unretrievable job and no resume path (re-invoking the tool submits a NEW job).

Suggest a larger budget for this dialect (e.g. 30–40 polls at a 15–30 s interval, 10–20 min ceiling) — the MiniMax comment about "~2 minutes worst case" does not transfer to OpenRouter's job durations.

comments.author: ai-teammate
comments.body:
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: video slot key resolution diverges from the image resolver and the new docs — silent empty-Authorization calls**

`resolveVideoGenerationEndpoint` requires `apiKeyName` and otherwise resolves to `''`, with two consequences for a plain override (no `useMainConnection`, no `apiKeyName`):

1. Unlike `resolveImageGenerationEndpoint` (`_resolveSlotKey` → `_isSameHost`), there is **no same-host reuse** of the main connection's key — yet `docs/media-models.md:31` (added in this PR) states the rule as "same-host reuse only, matching the CLI rule".
2. Unlike the image path, an empty key does **not** throw the actionable `MediaException` ("the imageGeneration slot has no resolvable API key …") — the video dialects just omit the `Authorization` header and the call fails later at the provider with a bare 401.

Since gh-1844 already rewrote this function's contract, please align it with the image resolver: same-host reuse plus a named, actionable error when no key resolves. If the divergence is intentional, the docs and the two resolvers' doc comments need to say so explicitly.

comments.author: ai-teammate
comments.body:
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: self-contradictory key-inheritance rule across docs / CLI / app**

This line says an override "never inherits the main provider's API key" **and** "(same-host reuse only, matching the CLI rule)" in the same sentence — those are two different policies, and the codebase now implements both:

- CLI image (`generate_image.dart` `_resolveSlotKey`): same-host reuse allowed.
- CLI video (`generate_video.dart`): no reuse, silent empty key.
- App store (`media_models_store.dart` `resolve`): "it NEVER inherits the main connection key" (its own comment).

So the docs assert a "CLI rule" that only one of the two CLI resolvers follows, and that the app deliberately does not. Please pick one policy per surface, make all three implementations agree, and rewrite this bullet to state it unambiguously (e.g. "the CLI allows same-host reuse of the main key; the app never inherits it — overrides there must name apiKeyName"). As written, users cannot tell which behavior to expect.

comments.author: ai-teammate
comments.body:
💡 **SUGGESTION: sanitize the file extension derived from `media_type`**

`ext` is `mediaType.substring('image/'.length)`, so a response with `media_type: "image/svg+xml"` (a real OpenRouter case, e.g. Recraft vector models — see the official image-generation docs) saves `generated/images/….svg+xml`. The bytes are fine, but the filename carries a `+`. Consider mapping known types (`png`, `jpeg`, `webp`, `svg`) and falling back to `png` otherwise.

comments.author: ai-teammate
comments.body:
💡 **SUGGESTION: `decide` is registered under the media facility bundle, though it has nothing to do with media**

The tool only needs the live main-connection accessors (`mainBaseUrl`/`mainProviderKind`/`mainApiKey`) — it ignores `modelsConfig`/`resolveKey`. Gating it on `services.media != null` means any host that wires no `MediaToolServices` (which exists for generate_image/generate_video) silently loses the `decide` tool, despite `agent_cli_tools.dart` declaring `'decide': on` unconditionally. Consider a small `DecisionsServices`-style bundle (or reusing a broader "main connection" seam) so the tool's availability doesn't depend on the media facility.

comments.author: ai-teammate
comments.body:
🚨 **BLOCKING: the shared picker's "Same as main connection" tile breaks `slot: null` flows — fa_ui shard 2 CI failure**

`MediaSlotProviderPickerPage` is shared by three flows: media slots (`slot: 'imageGeneration'` etc., via `media_models_section.dart`), task model roles (`slot: null`, via `task_models_section.dart`), and (with `allowMainConnection: false`) the default-chat flow. This change makes the tile unconditionally pop `MediaSlotEditorResult.save(MediaSlotOverride(useMainConnection: true))`.

For task model roles, `task_models_section.dart` treats a save result as a real override and persists `TaskRoleConfig(providerKind: '', baseUrl: '', modelId: '')` — the "Main connection" pick no longer clears the override. That is exactly the failing CI test (`task_models_section_test.dart:130`, "Main connection" clears the override — Expected: null, Actual: `TaskRoleConfig(, , )`).

Fix: only emit the opt-in save for actual media slots, e.g.

```dart
onTap: () => Navigator.of(context).pop(
  slot == null
      ? const MediaSlotEditorResult.clear()
      : const MediaSlotEditorResult.save(
          MediaSlotOverride(
            providerKind: '',
            baseUrl: '',
            modelId: '',
            useMainConnection: true,
          ),
        ),
),
```

and mirror the same `slot == null` condition in the `checked:` expression (`slot == null ? initial == null : (initial?.useMainConnection ?? false)`).

# Thread 5 — video slot key resolution diverges from the image resolver

`resolveVideoGenerationEndpoint` now matches the image resolver exactly
(gh-1844 review):

(TDD: RED first): same-host reuse returns the main key, cross-host/no-name

The docs bullet (thread 6) now states this one CLI rule explicitly.

comments.author: ai-teammate
comments.body:
# Thread 6 — self-contradictory key-inheritance rule across docs / CLI / app

Picked ONE policy per surface and made all implementations agree:

- **CLI** (`generate_image` + `generate_video`): same-host reuse of the
  main connection's key; a named-but-unresolvable or cross-host key throws
  the actionable "no resolvable API key" error before any provider call.
  Both resolvers now share the one helper (`resolveMediaSlotKey`), so the
  rule cannot drift again (thread 5's fix).
- **app** (`MediaModelsStore.resolve`): an override NEVER inherits the
  main connection's key — overrides must name `apiKeyName` (unchanged,
  matching the ticket's migration rule).

`docs/media-models.md` bullet rewritten unambiguously: the old "never
inherits … (same-host reuse only, matching the CLI rule)" single bullet is
replaced by an explicit per-surface list stating the CLI rule and the app
rule separately. Both resolvers' doc comments state the rule, and the app
store's comment already documented its no-inheritance policy.
